tldr: Headlines across the cluster center on the diplomatic shock of Russia's return to G20 in person and the European boycott it triggered — non-US press overwhelmingly leads with the invitation as a transatlantic affront rather than a peace signal. A secondary headline cluster, concentrated in Canadian and Russian-exile outlets, foregrounds the conditional wall Bessent erected: no economic relief until the Ukraine war ends.

silences.note: The Hindu's headline covers only India's attendance (Nirmala Sitharaman), carrying no detectable frame on Russia's reinstatement, European backlash, or war conditions.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to label European objections a 'tantrum', inverting the legitimacy of the boycott and casting Russia's G20 presence as a diplomatic win over EU opposition.
Only headline to mention that Bessent and Siluanov 'also talked about doing business again', surfacing an economic-normalisation angle absent from every other outlet's title.
Only headline to bundle Russia's invitation and press bans in a single clause, framing both as symptoms of the same US unilateralism rather than separate issues.
Only headline to lead with Bessent's 'back to basics' and Iran sanctions framing at the G20 opening, sidelining the Russia-Europe rift that dominates all non-US headline coverage.

bottom_line: Headline coverage advertises Russia's G20 reinstatement as an alliance rupture — the invitation, boycott, and backlash dominate above the fold — while sanctions-conditioned headlines from Canadian and Russian-exile outlets quietly carry the harder message Bessent delivered in the room.
